title: When the Hollow Burns Again
premise: Felix Ivensen has survived fifteen years of the crown's magic ban by selling charms too small to notice, but when a royal inquisitor begins burning guild members by name, she learns her late mother signed the covenant that once bound the human realm to the Hollow—and that covenant's failure is why winter never ends. Hunted across a freezing city, Felix must find the last three signatories' relics and reforge the pact before the solstice, even though doing so will strip every mage, including herself, of their gift forever. She succeeds at terrible cost: the Hollow's warmth returns, magic dies with her mother's line, and Felix—now ordinary—opens a shop selling nothing but candles.
about_author: Ada Ravensworth is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about people who inherit burdens they never asked for and live in cities that remember too much.

chapters.title: Charms Too Small to Notice
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In the frozen city of Vaelmoor, Felix sells luck-knots and warming sigils from a market stall, hiding her gift behind mundane wares. When the royal crier names the Iversen guild among those marked for the Hollow Hunt, an old client warns her the inquisitor already has her mother's ledger. The beat is dread disguised as routine—the life she built revealed as borrowed time.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Signatories
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, with a flashback interlude in her mother's voice. Fleeing to the guild's ruined hall, Felix deciphers the ledger and learns of the broken covenant with the Hollow and the three relics needed to reforge it. The inquisitor, Serah Vane, corners her there—not to kill her, but to offer a bargain: the relics for the other mages' lives. The beat is temptation; survival offered at others' expense.

chapters.title: What the Winter Keeps
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Felix and Serah Vane. Felix races through the dying city gathering the relics—a ring from a drowned friend, a bone-needle from a traitorous uncle, her own blood—while Vane's hunt burns the last guild members one by one. At the Hollow's threshold on solstice eve, Vane betrays the bargain, demanding the covenant name her as heir instead. The beat is betrayal at the climax's edge.

chapters.title: The Last Warm Thing
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. At the covenant stone, Felix refuses power entirely—she rewrites the pact as her mother should have, surrendering all magic, hers included, so the Hollow's warmth can flow freely to everyone. Vane, offered the same choice, grasps for the old terms and is unmade by the winter she served. The beat is grief transmuted into peace: spring's first thaw, and Felix lighting a plain candle in an ordinary shop.
